input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale:
Paragraph 4(a) is the only convenience-termination mechanic in the Agreement (no Exhibit-level term or separate early-termination-fee provision supplements it), and it sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred position, so it is not redlined.

Customer convenience right: expressed bilaterally rather than as a standalone Customer clause — "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — so we do hold a convenience right; a keyword check for a Customer-specific convenience sentence is a phrasing artifact only. Notice is 90 days, the outer edge of the 60-90 day fallback window.

Committed lock-in: a single 12-month Initial Term, which is not "longer than 12 months", so the missing-behaviour deviation test for absence of a Customer convenience right during a multi-year commitment is not triggered.

Vendor right: correcting my earlier characterisation, Kubient's right is not strictly end-of-term — "following the Initial Term" would also permit exit mid-renewal-term on 90 days' notice. That is slightly broader than the fallback's "end of a term" formulation, but it remains within fallback tolerance because the notice period is a full 90 days (so it does not reach the walk-away test of Vendor convenience termination on fewer than 90 days), Kubient cannot exit at all during the Initial Term, and the right is exactly symmetrical with ours, giving us the same mid-renewal flexibility.

No penalty: Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is consideration for services actually delivered during the 90-day notice window and in any event does not exceed the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling.

Noted but not flagged (minor sub-elements short of preferred): no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on termination, and no ability to terminate individual Exhibits in part. Worth raising as drafting comments only if this clause is reopened.
